claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase bcc HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy in a random-solid-solution or low-SRO state.
Single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloys can have a significant energetic driving force for chemical short-range order.
Controlled annealing can evolve SRO from isolated clusters into a percolated network while preserving a single phase.
Above 800 K, SRO remains stable while long-range ordering is suppressed.
The phonon mean free path is comparable to the spacing between SRO clusters in the proposed regime.
At low SRO volume fractions, isolated SRO clusters increase phonon scattering and reduce thermal conductivity.
Percolation of SRO clusters creates continuous low-scattering pathways through the alloy.
Coherent vibrational modes along an ordered SRO network reduce phonon scattering.
The net dependence of thermal conductivity on SRO is non-monotonic.
The critical SRO volume fraction for the proposed transition is approximately 0.3-0.4.
Thermal conductivity exhibits a sharp percolative jump or slope change at the critical SRO fraction.
Above the percolation threshold, conductivity increases or stabilizes despite increasing SRO density.
SRO-cluster percolation explains why serial, parallel, Maxwell-Eucken, or effective-medium mixing models fail to predict the conductivity change.
Prior fcc literature predicts a monotonic reduction in thermal conductivity with increasing SRO because of enhanced phonon scattering.
Standard interatomic potential functions may fail to reproduce the correct SRO evolution and cluster connectivity.
The exact percolation threshold and conductivity change depend on the interatomic potential's representation of cluster-formation energetics.
The proposed mechanism applies only if SRO percolates without phase decomposition, long-range ordering, or precipitation.
The proposed mechanism fails when the phonon mean free path is much larger than the percolation correlation length.
APT combined with in-situ conductivity measurements can test whether cluster connectivity coincides with a conductivity jump or slope change.
A DFT-validated machine-learning interatomic potential can be used to simulate the proposed SRO-dependent phonon-transport test.
